deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): X is a space stratified by a closed stratum Y with open complement X* = X∖Y. V_{Y,X} is a tubular neighbourhood of Y, homotopic to Y, and U*_{Y,X} (also written V*_{Y,X}) is the deleted tubular neighbourhood. When the 'building pieces' Y, X*, U* are K(π,1)'s, the data are a diagram of fundamental groups π1(Y) ← π1(U*) → π1(X*), the diagrams (7)/(8)/(10) and the homomorphisms (13).

On the previous page Grothendieck builds a topos F out of this diagram. He tests it on the simplest cell decomposition of S^2: Y = a point, X* ≅ C, U* ≅ punctured disc, so the diagram is 1 ← Z → 1. There F is equivalent to presheaves on •→•, which is contractible, while S^2 is not. So F, which seemed to 'take account of' the π1 of the pieces, does not give the homotopy type of X, and the canonical map X → F is not a homotopy equivalence.

On this page he first records a fear: under the K(π,1) hypotheses, perhaps the homotopy type of X cannot be recovered at all from the homotopy types of X*, Y, U* and the diagrams. He then states that the fear is unfounded; it is only F that is inadequate for expressing the correct homotopy type. In modern terms, X is the homotopy pushout of Y ← U* → X*, which depends only on the diagram of homotopy types, here of groups; for 1 ← Z → 1 one gets ΣS^1 = S^2. F is evidently not that homotopy colimit.

To demonstrate this he recovers H^2(X,A), A a commutative coefficient group, from diagram (23). He reads H^2(X,A) as classifying A-gerbes on X and starts invoking descent ('recollement') for gerbes on topoi. Completed on the next page, the argument is:
- an A-gerbe on X is a gerbe on X*, a gerbe on V_{Y,X}, and an equivalence of their restrictions to V*;
- on a connected K(π,1), an A-gerbe is a central extension of π by A;
- so a gerbe on X amounts to extensions of π1(Y) and of π1(X*) by A, plus an isomorphism of their pullbacks to D = π1(U*).
This works when the pieces are connected with π2 = 0.

For S^2 (completing his computation): both extensions of the trivial group are trivial. The gluing isomorphisms of the trivial extension A×Z are classified by Hom(Z,A) = A. Hence H^2(S^2,A) = A, which is the Mayer–Vietoris connecting map H^1(D*,A) → H^2(S^2,A) in non-abelian, gerbe-theoretic dress.
errors: No mathematical error on this page itself. The page records that the earlier construction F was the wrong model: F fails to be the homotopy pushout of 1 ← BZ → 1.

Implicit hypotheses needed for the gerbe argument: A abelian with trivial lien (so extensions are central), and descent of gerbes along the cover {X*, V_{Y,X}}. Strictly, H^2 classifies equivalence classes of gerbes, so automorphisms of the pieces' extensions must be quotiented out when counting gluings. Grothendieck states the connectedness and π2 = 0 conditions on the next page.

ideas.what: The homotopy type of a stratified space whose strata and deleted tubular neighbourhoods are K(π,1)'s is determined by the diagram of fundamental groups π1(Y) ← π1(U*) → π1(X*); the naive topos of the diagram is not the right model
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy pushout / homotopy colimit of a diagram of classifying spaces (Seifert–van Kampen for homotopy types); dévissage of stratified homotopy types
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical homotopy theory (homotopy colimits: Segal, Bousfield–Kan, Vogt, Thomason); stratified version: MacPherson, Quinn, Treumann, Lurie (exit paths)
ideas.where_published: Themes of dévissage of stratified spaces appear in Esquisse d'un programme (1984). Homotopy types modelled by stacks appear in Pursuing Stacks (1983).

ideas.what: Computing H^2(X,A) by interpreting it as classifying A-gerbes and gluing gerbes along an open cover / tubular neighbourhood
ideas.where_published: Gerbe ideas originate with Grothendieck and were developed by Giraud; stacks of gerbes figure in Pursuing Stacks.

ideas.what: On a K(π,1), A-gerbes correspond to (central) extensions of π by A
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Schreier, Eilenberg–MacLane); Giraud for the gerbe formulation

missed.claim: A dated (c.1981) record of Grothendieck finding that a naive topos attached to a diagram of K(π,1) strata loses homotopy information (S^2 comes out contractible), and turning to gerbe/2-stack descent to recover it. This is a small historical precursor of the motivation for Pursuing Stacks: modelling homotopy types by higher stacks rather than by topoi of diagrams of groups.
missed.quote: si le topos F n'est pas suffisant, bien, pour exprimer le type d'homotopie correct ... J'interprète H^2(X,A) comme classifiant les gerbes sur X liées par A
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest for the genesis of stratified homotopy theory and of Pursuing Stacks. Mathematically, it is standard today.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct but standard: the homotopy-pushout principle and gerbe descent computing H^2(S^2). The only interest is historical, as a 1981 trace of the step from topoi of diagrams to higher-stack descent in the stratified setting.
transcription_corrections: 'si le topos F n'en pas suffisant' should read 'si le topos F n'est pas suffisant'.
The insertion 'K(π,1)' belongs in 'sous les hypothèses K(π,1) faites'. The insertion 'de X' belongs in 'le type d'homotopie de X'.
'groupe de coeff commun' is likely 'groupe de coeff commutatif'.
The final line reads 'une théorie de recollement' (word split across the page). The insertion is 'pour des gerbes sur des topos' (replacing a struck word).
